item.title: Video: ‘We love you’ – Fountain of Life Church members give Jimmy Odukoya rousing welcome
item.description: Members of the Fountain of Life Church have welcomed their senior pastor, Jimmy Odukoya, with cheers and chants of affection during Sunday service, days after a dispute over his leadership of the church became a subject of litigation. In a video from the service, Odukoya took the stage to applause from the congregation, who repeatedly chanted, “We love you.” 'We love you' — Fountain of Life Church members chant as Jimmy Odukoya takes the stage pic.twitter.com/YXNZljrfMv — TheCable (@thecableng) November 22, 2026 Responding to the reception, he said, “Fountain, I love you.” He added, “We have a lot to talk about, but first of all, we have a pleasant surprise this morning, Bishop Mike decided to surprise us this morning. Please welcome to the stage Bishop Mike Okonkwo.” The welcome came amid an ongoing leadership dispute at the church, which has seen rival positions emerge over Odukoya’s status as senior pastor. On Friday, Odukoya approached the Federal High Court in Lagos, challenging his reported removal as senior pastor and questioning the legality of decisions allegedly taken by some members of the church’s Board of Trustees. The suit, instituted alongside the Incorporated Trustees of The Fountain of Life Church, named his sister, Tolu Odukoya, and seven other church leaders as respondents. They include Pastors Rotimi Okpaise, Tobi Enuha, Gbenga Onabanjo, Fred Ohiani and Akin Osinbajo, as well as Biodun Balogun and Biodun Awosika. Odukoya is challenging the validity of meetings held by some trustees on January 22, February 28 and November 16, 2026, and the decisions allegedly reached at those meetings. He is also asking the court to determine whether the trustees could remove him as senior pastor without following the procedures stipulated in the church’s constitution. The dispute became public on November 17 when a group identifying itself as members of the church’s Board of Trustees announced that Odukoya was no longer recognised as senior pastor, with immediate effect. The group reportedly cited a review of the church’s constitution and succession instructions allegedly left by the late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, who died in August 2023. The trustees subsequently named Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader pending consultations and the establishment of a substantive leadership structure. However, the church rejected the announcement, insisting that Jimmy Odukoya remained its duly appointed senior pastor and chairman of the Board of Trustees. The disagreement took another turn on November 18 when the Lagos State High Court granted interim orders restraining Odukoya from presenting himself as the church’s senior pastor and spiritual head. Justice O.O. Adewunmi-Oshin also restrained him from interfering with or disrupting the church’s governance and administration. item.title: School building collapses, kills pupil in Abia
item.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA -Tragedy struck at Ehere Community Primary School, in Obingwa LGA, Abia State, last Friday, when a pupil, identified as Vincent Chiedozie Dum, was reportedly killed by a collapsed building at the school. Nine other pupils escaped death as they fled before the collapse of the building. The deceased, a primary two pupil,was said to have gone to ease himself beside the dilapidated building when the wall suddenly collapsed on him. Principal of Ehere Community Senior Secondary School, Mr. Nwogu Chioma Allen, said they have been warning the pupils and students about the dangers of going around the dilapidated buildings in the compound. Nwogu stated the deceased pupil was rescued and taken to three hospitals who rejected for medical attention. However, he said the boy was later admitted at the Abia State University Teaching Hospital, ABSUTH, Aba. He also disclosed that about 10 pupils and students were playing around the building when it suddenly collapsed and hit the victim while the pupils escaped. The Principal said; “This place contains five institutions; the Ministry of Education, Primary Schools 1 and 2 and Ehere Community Junior and Senior Secondary Schools. We have a building here that is very weak. The building over the years, has lost its strength. You know children, they have been running around and we have been chasing them , telling them not to go around the building. “Unfortunately, that afternoon, they were running around the place, up to 10 of them went , running around that building. My teachers were shouting to them, leave that area. Incidentally, the building fell on the boy, the other children were able to escape. The boy was taken to three hospitals for medical attention, but they all rejected him.” He urged the state government to extend it’s school rehabilitation projects to the Ehere Community Primary and Secondary School. “Some of the buildings here are weak. The government has been trying in the renovation of schools. We hope that our own school will be renovated to avert such situations.” When Vanguard visited the school, it was observed that the dilapidated building has been sealed off. The post School building collapses, kills pupil in Abia appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: First-Class degree not enough to make excellent teacher – TRCN
item.description: The Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria (TRCN) says possessing a first-class degree does not automatically make an individual an excellent teacher. Dr. Ronke Soyombo, Registrar/Chief Executive of TRCN, stated this in an interview with Newsmen on Sunday in Abuja. Soyombo stressed the importance of professional competence adding that effective teaching required more than academic qualifications. The registrar explained that teachers must demonstrate competence in five critical areas assessed through the Council’s professional qualifying examination. She identified the areas as basic mathematics, foundational literacy, digital literacy, pedagogy, and safeguarding and child protection. According to her, teachers must possess a sound understanding of basic mathematical concepts to effectively support children’s learning and development. She described foundational literacy as equally important, noting that strong literacy skills enabled teachers to support learning across other subject areas. The registrar said teachers must also understand today’s children, particularly those belonging to the Alpha Generation, and the technological environment in which they operate. She identified digital literacy as the third major area of assessment, describing it as compulsory for teachers seeking to engage effectively with contemporary learners. To illustrate the challenge, Soyombo recalled visiting an examination centre where she encountered an elderly teacher struggling with a computer mouse. “I remember visiting an examination centre recently and meeting an elderly teacher who held a computer mouse and asked me, ‘Madam, what am I going to do with this?’” she said. She said the encounter highlighted the extent of digital literacy challenges confronting some teachers and raised concerns about their preparedness for modern classrooms. “How can teachers effectively engage children in today’s classrooms if they are not comfortable with basic technology?” she asked. Soyombo, however, acknowledged the challenges and disclosed that several training programmes were being implemented to improve teachers’ digital competence. On pedagogy, she said possessing excellent academic qualifications did not automatically translate into the ability to teach effectively. “Having a first-class degree does not automatically make someone an excellent teacher,” she said. She explained that academic qualifications alone could not guarantee that a teacher understood how to apply appropriate instructional methods to address different learning needs. According to her, classrooms comprise learners with varying abilities, including average pupils, children requiring additional support, and gifted and talented learners. item.title: Full list: FG announces 19 international job vacancies [How to apply]
item.description: The Federal Government, FG has announced 19 international job vacancies for qualified Nigerians at the African Space Agency and the General Secretariat of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC). The vacancies, announced by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, comprise five positions at the African Space Agency headquarters in Cairo, Egypt, and 14 positions at the OIC headquarters in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. The ministry disclosed this in two separate vacancy announcements dated Friday, November 20, 2026, signed by its spokesperson, Oluwafemi Adeniyi, and shared on its official Facebook page on Saturday. According to the ministry, the African Space Agency is recruiting for five positions, with application deadlines of November 25 and December 10, 2026. The positions include Director, Corporate Services (D-1); Director-General, African Space Agency (D-2); Head of Legal Affairs (Grade P-5); Senior Finance Officer (P3); and Senior Human Resources Officer (P3). The ministry said interested and qualified Nigerians should visit the agency’s official website at https://africanspaceagency.org for details of the eligibility requirements and application procedures. For the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation, the ministry announced 14 vacancies across its departments and specialised units. The positions include Director-General of Political Affairs; Director, Administration Department; Director, Information Department; Director, Conference Department; Director, Muslim Communities and Minorities; Director, African Affairs; and Director, European Affairs and International Organisations. Others are Head of Human Resources (PP2); Professional Officer, Human Resources (PP2); Professional Officers, Administration Department (P2); Director, Peace, Security and Mediation Unit; Chief of HRC Office – IUT; Registrar – IUT; and Deputy Internal Auditor – IUT. The ministry said the application deadlines for the OIC positions range from November 29 to December 24, 2026. It urged interested and qualified Nigerians to visit the organisation’s official vacancy portal at https://www.oic-oci.org/en/vacancies for information on the specific requirements, application procedures and deadlines for each position. How to apply Interested Nigerians can apply through the following official platforms: African Space Agency: Visit https://africanspaceagency.org , navigate to the recruitment or careers section, and check the available positions, eligibility criteria and application instructions. Organisation of Islamic Cooperation: Visit https://www.oic-oci.org/en/vacancies , select the relevant vacancy and follow the stated application procedure. Applicants are advised to review the requirements for their preferred positions and submit their applications before the respective deadlines. item.title: Dickson mourns victims of Bayelsa boat mishap, seeks safety measures
item.description: Former Governor of Bayelsa State, Senator Henry Seriake Dickson, has commiserated with the families and friends of victims of the boat mishap along the Ayama/Oweikorogha waterways in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of the state. Dickson, who disclosed this in a post on his X platform on Sunday, described the incident as unfortunate and expressed sadness over the loss of lives. He also extended his condolences to the Bayelsa State Government and the people of the state over the tragedy. The senator said he deliberately scaled down his engagements on Saturday as a mark of respect for those who lost their lives in the incident. According to him, he reduced the number of visitors he attended to and cancelled some previously scheduled visits to reflect on the tragedy. Dickson commended the relevant emergency response agencies and other individuals involved in the rescue operation for their swift response, urging them to sustain their efforts until the operation was successfully concluded. He also called for stricter enforcement of maritime safety regulations and increased public awareness to prevent similar incidents. The former governor stressed the need for continuous safety education for marine operators, security personnel and residents of Bayelsa State. He further urged traditional institutions and the media to support efforts aimed at promoting maritime safety and ensuring compliance with relevant regulations. Dickson reiterated his condolences to the bereaved families, praying that God would grant the deceased eternal rest and give their loved ones the strength to bear the loss. item.title: PSG star Doue in tears after suffering worrying knee injury against Nice
item.description: Paris Saint-Germain star Desire Doue was stretchered off in tears after suffering what looked like a nasty knee injury as the reigning French and European champions beat Nice 3-2 in Ligue 1 on Saturday. Doue went down after twisting awkwardly late in the first half as he tried to control the ball, shortly after scoring to put PSG 2-1 ahead. He looked in agony as he clutched his right knee, and the match was stopped for five minutes to allow Doue to receive treatment before being carried off to a backdrop of applause from the crowd at the Allianz Riviera stadium. PSG will now be dreading discovering the extent of the injury, having lost Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee playing against Barcelona last month. The Georgian winger is unlikely to return this season, and Doue looks set for a significant spell on the sidelines too. “We will need to wait until tomorrow for the test results, but it is obviously a serious injury,” PSG coach Luis Enrique told broadcaster Ligue 1+. The 21-year-old French international, who can play on the wing or in midfield, has been arguably PSG’s best player this season after playing a key role in their Champions League triumphs in each of the last two campaigns. He has notably scored three goals in three Champions League appearances this season for PSG, who sold Bradley Barcola to Liverpool at the beginning of the campaign and have seen Ousmane Dembele struggle with his fitness recently. – ‘Not a problem’ – “This is the life of a professional player at the very highest level,” added Luis Enrique. “You just have to accept it and I am sure he will find a way to recover well and come back even stronger.” Asked about the possibility of moving to sign a replacement in the January transfer window, the Spanish coach said PSG were “always open to possibilities”. “We have players who can come in and we will overcome this as a team. It is not a problem,” he added. Earlier, Algerian international Mohamed Amoura had given Nice the lead only for Senny Mayulu to equalise with a penalty awarded after a VAR check following a handball in the home box. Doue — who was wearing a mouthguard after one of his teeth became dislodged while playing for France against Italy during the international break — put PSG ahead a minute after that goal, turning in at the back post from an Achraf Hakimi assist for his sixth of the season in all competitions. His replacement Ferran Torres scored PSG’s third in the 85th minute, controlling in the box before finishing on the turn for his eighth goal of the season — but first in two months. Ali Abdi pulled one back for Nice in stoppage time, but their run of three straight wins was ended as PSG made it 12 victories on the bounce. Eight of those wins have come in Ligue 1, in which PSG are now five points clear at the top from Lille, who lost 1-0 at home to Lyon with Mads Bidstrup scoring the only goal. item.title: COP31 faces collapse threat as latest draft fails to mention fossil fuels
item.description: The COP31 presidency proposed an eleventh-hour deal Sunday that again fails to mention fossil fuels — an omission that deepened a tense standoff at the UN climate talks. The latest offering by summit co-hosts Turkey and Australia published deep into overtime leaves unresolved tensions over planet-heating fossil fuels but retains a much-sought goal to electrify the global economy. The proposal needs consensus approval from nearly 200 nations at a closing session Sunday but they have struggled to bridge differences during two weeks of grinding negotiations. The European Union and other nations have pushed for strong language on transitioning away from fossil fuels, a call that has faced resistance from oil-rich Saudi Arabia. An EU official told AFP the latest proposal was a “backwards” step, warning there was a “very real possibility” that COP31 ends with no deal. “I am more pessimistic today than I was yesterday,” the official said on condition of anonymity. “The situation is difficult, and the outcome is uncertain. The oil-producing countries are putting up a fierce fight,” a German official said. A Saudi official declined to comment when approached by AFP. Fossil fuels are a flashpoint at the climate talks and the summit comes against a difficult backdrop of soaring energy prices and geopolitical tensions stemming from the war in Iran. A draft deal unveiled earlier this week called for a faster phase out of fossil fuels but a second, pared-down version released Thursday stripped away all mentions of coal, oil and gas. Threats of a walkout prompted Turkey and Australia to convene a hurried meeting between the European Union and Saudi Arabia in a bid to broker a compromise. The latest text introduces a reference to a previous global deal in 2023 to shift the world away from fossil fuels — but stops short of naming them explicitly. And it retains a contentious push to expand carbon capture and storage, a technology championed by the fossil fuel industry but criticised as costly and ineffective in cutting emissions. “We are very disappointed with how the text looks,” the environment minister of Antigua and Barbuda, Michael Joseph, told AFP after leaving the COP31 presidency’s offices. “I can’t honestly say that I’m okay with it passing” in its current state, Joseph said, adding that the draft was “quite silent” on fossil fuels. – Goal to electrify – The draft also calls for global efforts to boost the share of electricity in total final energy consumption to 35 percent by 2035 and the expansion of “clean energy”. The summit had been under pressure to show progress in tackling soaring greenhouse gas emissions in a year of climate-linked disasters from Europe to Nepal and Indonesia. Facing blowback over fossil fuels, Turkey and Australia pointed to “electrification” as a way to cut heat-trapping emissions and bolster energy security. item.title: Kwara jailbreak: 20 officers queried as investigation reveals escape plans
item.description: By Demola Akinyemi Ilorin About 20 officers of the Medium Security Custodial Centre, Oke-Kura, in Ilorin, Kwara State, are being investigated over last Wednesday’s jailbreak by two condemned inmates. Vanguard reliably gathered that among those now facing scrutiny are members of the armed squad and duty officers on round-the-clock supervision of inmates at the facility. According to dependable sources (names withheld), probes indicate that last Wednesday’s jailbreak was a larger, coordinated effort involving seven inmates. According to insider accounts, the inmates spent months secretly chiseling through the wall of their cell without prison management detecting it, pasting a poster over the opening to conceal the gradual breach. On the morning of the escape, the convicts were said to have tied blankets to make a makeshift rope, throwing it to hook the broken bottles on the high perimeter fence. “While the first two convicts successfully scaled the wall and fled, the rope snapped under the weight of the remaining five inmates, sending them falling back,” the source hinted. Contacted,the Spokesperson of the state command, Adegbulugbe Phillips Olumide, however, could not confirm the development. “I cannot confirm the report; those who came to investigate the incident returned to Abuja yesterday,so there’s no report on the outcome yet.”he said Recall that the Controller General of Nigerian Correctional Service Sylvester Nwakuche,who visited the scene on Thursday, attributed the escape of two condemned prison inmates to negligence, describing the incident as unfortunate and unacceptable. Nwakuche also vowed that staff found guilty in the incident would be dealt with severely. He, however, assured that a security dragnet has been spread across the state and the country and that the two escaped condemned criminals would be rearrested. Meanwhile, the inmates identified as Shegun and Abraham, who reportedly escaped on Wednesday after breaking and scaling the wall of the custodial centre to ease their escape, have been declared wanted by the centre. item.title: Messi deserved red card for throwing ball at opponent, says Columbus coach
item.description: Columbus Crew coach Laurent Courtois said Lionel Messi should have been sent off after hurling a throw-in at an opponent as Inter Miami crashed to a 3-0 defeat in the MLS Cup playoffs on Saturday. Messi’s frustration boiled over on the stroke of half-time when he aimed a forceful throw-in into the face of Columbus Crew forward Gonzalo Tapia with 10-man Miami trailing 1-0 at the time. Messi and Tapia both were shown yellow cards for the incident by referee Allen Chapman, but Courtois said afterwards the Argentina superstar should have been given a red card. “Everybody knows that he deserved more than a yellow card,” Courtois said in a post-game press conference when asked about the incident. “It’s just really sad.” Referee Chapman later defended the decision to only show Messi a yellow. “The force used was negligible and the offense did not reach the level of violent conduct,” Chapman told a pool reporter. Inter Miami had already been reduced to 10 men when the incident occurred and were 1-0 down after Chile international Tapia’s early penalty. Reigning MLS champions Miami went on to suffer a 3-0 defeat, with Tapia grabbing a second after a Taha Habroune strike just after half-time at Miami’s Nu Stadium. The result means seventh seeds Columbus, the 2023 champions, can eliminate Messi and Miami from the playoffs with a victory in game two of the best-of-three series in Ohio next Friday. “It was a game where nothing went right for us, and we effectively created their chances for them,” Miami coach Kily Gonzalez said afterwards. “We didn’t produce the great performance we had hoped for. Everything went wrong, but we have to learn from it because next time, if we don’t win, we’re out,” he added. “There’s no better challenge for us as a team than this. It’s a test of character, and I know my team has that character.” In other MLS playoff action on Saturday, Joaquin Valiente scored two goals as host Dallas beat Portland 3-0 in their Western Conference series opener. The 25-year-old Uruguayan midfielder scored in the 53rd and 55th minutes and Samuel Sarver added an insurance goal in the fourth minute of stoppage time for Dallas, who can advance by winning at Portland next Saturday. US teen Peyton Miller scored one goal and set up another in New England’s 2-0 victory over visiting Philadelphia. Miller’s 10th-minute shot deflected in off Philadelphia defender Nathan Harriel to make it 1-0 and the 19-year-old scored in the 73rd minute off a Jack Harrison cross to complete the scoring. New England can advance to the MLS Eastern Conference semi-finals with a road victory next Saturday. item.title: Troops raid bandits’ hideout in Kogi, recover AK-47 rifles
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of the Nigerian Army have dislodged suspected armed bandits from a hideout in Kogi State, recovering two AK-47 rifles, three magazines and 65 rounds of ammunition during an intelligence-led operation. The operation, conducted on Saturday, November 21, 2026, targeted suspected kidnappers operating in the Osara, Gada and Ohakiti forest areas of Okehi Local Government Area, following intelligence reports on their activities and hideouts. In a statement, the Acting Director, Army Public Relations, Colonel Appolonia Anele, said the operation was launched by troops deployed from Patrol Base Kabba in collaboration with other security personnel. She said the operation was aimed at dismantling criminal hideouts linked to the recent spate of kidnappings along the Kabba–Okene Road and neighbouring communities. According to the statement, troops encountered about six armed bandits at an abandoned settlement within the forest during the offensive, engaging them and forcing them to flee. A subsequent search of the hideout led to the recovery of two AK-47 rifles, three magazines and 65 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition. Other items recovered from the enclave included bags, torchlights, food supplies and a power bank believed to have been used by the fleeing suspects. The Army said the operation underscored its determination to deny criminal elements freedom of action, dismantle their operational bases and restore security along vulnerable routes and communities in Kogi State. It reaffirmed its commitment to sustaining intelligence-driven operations in collaboration with other security agencies to eliminate threats to lives and property. The Army also urged members of the public to continue providing timely and credible information to security agencies to support ongoing efforts to identify and clear hideouts used by criminal elements across the country. The post Troops raid bandits’ hideout in Kogi, recover AK-47 rifles appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ‘I Struggled To Come Out, Lost My Sister, Other Relatives,’ Bayelsa Boat Accident Survivor
item.description: A survivor of Friday’s boat accident in the Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has recounted how she struggled to escape from the capsized vessel, saying she lost several members of her family and neighbours in the tragedy. The woman, whose identity was not immediately disclosed, said her elder sister, her sister’s daughter-in-law and two children belonging to her relatives and neighbours were among those who died in the accident. Recounting the incident, she said the boat suddenly capsized, trapping passengers beneath it. “The boat just fell and pressed all of us. My elder sister’s son’s wife was lost. My elder sister was lost. Her son was also lost. One of my neighbours who followed us also lost her son. My neighbour herself was lost,” she said. ﻿ The survivor said she was the only person among those close to her who made it out alive, adding that she struggled to escape after the boat overturned. “It’s only me that is safe. When I came out, somebody held me. I was drinking water. I was not able to come out. I struggled before I came out. Where we were standing, the boat broke from above and pressed us down,” she said. Asked by the Bayelsa governor, Douye Diri, whether the bodies of her missing relatives and neighbours had been recovered, she replied in the negative. Her account comes as the death toll from the accident has risen to 23, while 24 survivors are receiving treatment in hospitals. The accident occurred near Oweikorogha Community in the Ukubie area of Southern Ijaw when a boat conveying mourners from Ayama Community to Ukubie for a burial ceremony capsized at about 11 a.m. on Friday. ﻿ The Bayelsa State Police Command confirmed the incident, saying preliminary findings indicated that the boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways. However, a survivor had also alleged that the wooden passenger vessel, popularly known as a ‘love boat’, was overloaded with passengers and their belongings, raising concerns about possible breaches of waterway safety regulations. President Bola Tinubu has expressed condolences to the families of the victims and directed relevant federal disaster response agencies to support rescue and recovery operations. In a statement posted on his X account, Tinubu described the incident as tragic and said those who died did not deserve to lose their lives in such circumstances. “Those who lost their lives in the tragedy did not deserve to die that way. I have directed all relevant Federal Disaster Response agencies to work together to ensure a successful recovery and rescue operation,” he said. The President also directed that Saturday’s presidential campaign rally in Ibadan, Oyo State, be held without much fanfare in honour of the victims. Meanwhile, Governor Diri has visited the scene of the accident and is expected to initiate an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the tragedy. item.title: Can Enzo Maresca Win The Premier League In His First Season At Man City?
item.description: Six league titles. Ten years. A stand at the Etihad with his name on it. Good luck following that. Enzo Maresca has to, after Manchester City unveiled him as manager back in June 2026. Maresca at least knows his way around the training ground. Back in 2020-2021, he ran the Elite Development Squad and won Premier League 2 with them. He returned in 2022 to work under Guardiola as an assistant, and that season ended with the treble. So this is spell number three, and he’s tied down until 2029. Expectations at City don’t reset just because the man in the dugout has changed. City’s title odds have become some of the most debated in premier league online betting markets because bookmakers must weigh a campaign shaped as much by events off the pitch as on it. A Flying Start, Then A Bump The opening weeks went better than almost anyone expected. Maresca became the first manager in Premier League history to win his first seven games in charge of a new club. The football looked familiar too. City kept the ball and wore teams down, which is no surprise from a coach who learned so much from Guardiola. His Leicester and Chelsea sides played the same way. City spent big to help him. Their summer outlay of around £460 million was a record for any club, and £125 million of it went on Enzo Fernández from Chelsea, a fee that matched the Premier League transfer record. Phil Foden signed a four-year extension. Rodri, one of the faces of the Guardiola years, left for Barcelona. Maresca has won quickly before. He lifted the Championship title with Leicester in 2023-24. A year later at Chelsea, he won the Conference League and the Club World Cup and still finished fourth in the league. Seven straight wins at the start of a season guarantee nothing, of course. Plenty of fast starters have slid down the Premier League table once the winter fixtures arrive. City soon lost three league games in a row, one of them a 1-0 home defeat to Brighton, who had never won away at City before. Then there are Arsenal. Mikel Arteta, another former Guardiola assistant, ended their 22-year wait for the title in 2025-26, helped along by a Premier League record for goals from corners. Manchester City’s Italian manager Enzo Maresca gestures on the touchline during the English Premier League football match between Manchester City and Sunderland at the Etihad Stadium in Manchester, north west England, on September 20, 2026. (Photo by PETER POWELL / AFP) The Fight Off the Pitch The bigger problem might be off the pitch entirely. Early in the 2026-27 season, an independent commission found City guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules. It ruled that the club used “sham” contracts with commercial partners to inflate revenues and cut costs by more than £900 million between 2009 and 2018. City deny any wrongdoing and have appealed. item.title: Death Toll In Bayelsa Boat Accident Rises To 23
item.description: The death toll from Friday’s boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has risen to 23, with 24 survivors receiving treatment in hospitals. The accident occurred when a boat conveying mourners to a burial ceremony capsized near Oweikorogha Community in the Ukubie area of Southern Ijaw. The Bayelsa State Police Command confirmed the incident in a statement, saying the boat was travelling from Ayama Community to Ukubie for a burial ceremony on Friday, when it capsized at about 11 a.m. A preliminary police report indicated that the boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways. Following the incident, rescue operations were launched, with several passengers rescued while others were initially reported missing. A survivor had also alleged that the wooden passenger boat, popularly known as a ‘love boat’, was overloaded with passengers and their belongings, suggesting that this might have contributed to the accident. President Bola Tinubu has expressed condolences to the families of the victims, describing the incident as tragic and directing relevant federal disaster response agencies to support rescue and recovery efforts. In a statement posted on his X account, Tinubu said, “Those who lost their lives in the tragedy did not deserve to die that way. I have directed all relevant Federal Disaster Response agencies to work together to ensure a successful recovery and rescue operation.” The President also directed that the presidential campaign rally in Ibadan, Oyo State, on Saturday, be held without much fanfare in honour of those who lost their lives. “On behalf of the entire nation, I mourn those who lost their lives in the incident and sympathise with their families, the government and the people of Bayelsa State. “I particularly mourn with Governor Douye Diri over this sad incident. I pray that God Almighty repose their souls and comfort their families,” he said. Meanwhile, Governor Douye Diri has visited the scene of the accident and is expected to initiate a probe into the circumstances surrounding the tragedy. The state government has also warned boat operators against overloading, reckless navigation and travelling without life jackets, stressing the need for strict compliance with waterway safety regulations. item.title: China Diaries: The Railway Connecting Continents
item.description: Standing at the Xi’an International Port Station in northwest China, watching the movement of freight trains preparing to transport goods across borders and continents, I was reminded that economic development is not only about what a country produces. It is also about how efficiently it can move what it produces to the rest of the world. Xi’an occupies an interesting place in China’s history. It was once the starting point of the ancient Silk Road, which connected China to Central Asia, the Middle East and Europe through centuries of trade and cultural exchange. Today, the city is reclaiming that historic role through a modern railway network that connects Chinese manufacturing centres to markets across Europe and Asia. The China-Europe Railway Express is one of the most visible outcomes of China’s Belt and Road Initiative (BRI). Through this network, freight trains transport automobiles, electronics, machinery, textiles, agricultural products and other goods across the Eurasian continent. What makes the initiative particularly interesting is how it has transformed the economic possibilities of a city located thousands of kilometres from the sea. Xi’an has become an important international logistics hub, demonstrating that geographical distance from a coastline does not have to limit a city’s participation in global trade. The railway network has continued to expand. By November 2025, China-Europe freight trains had completed nearly 120,000 journeys, connecting 232 cities in 26 European countries and more than 100 cities in 11 Asian countries. The value of goods transported through the network had reached $426.4 billion by the end of 2024. These are not merely impressive transportation figures. They represent an evolving system of economic connectivity, linking manufacturers, suppliers, distributors and consumers across national borders. Beyond transportation: The economics of connectivity The significance of the railway goes beyond moving containers from one destination to another. It creates opportunities for businesses to reach markets faster, diversify their supply chains and reduce their dependence on a single transportation route. Rail freight offers an important middle ground between air and sea transportation. While it is generally more expensive than shipping by sea, it can be considerably faster. For certain categories of goods, particularly machinery, automobile components, electronics and other time-sensitive products, that difference can be commercially significant. It also provides an alternative when disruptions affect other transportation routes. Another important feature is the development of inland logistics infrastructure. Warehousing, customs processing, container handling, industrial parks and distribution services have grown around railway connections. item.title: Chelsea Humbled As Leeds Run Riot
item.description: Chelsea suffered an embarrassing 4-1 defeat against Leeds on Saturday as the Blues were beaten for the third time in their last four Premier League matches. Xabi Alonso’s side were ripped apart by rampant Leeds, who savoured their first Premier League win at Stamford Bridge in 27 years. Chelsea scored six in a League Cup win against Leeds in September, but Daniel Farke’s men erased that painful result with a superb display on their return to West London. Just 24 hours after NFL legend Tom Brady was linked with buying a minority stake in Chelsea, the seven-time Super Bowl winner might be thinking twice about his mooted investment. Leeds United’s English goalkeeper #01 James Trafford and Leeds United’s Swiss striker #19 Noah Okafor celebrate after the English Premier League football match between Chelsea and Leeds United at Stamford Bridge in London on November 21, 2026. (Photo by Henry NICHOLLS / AFP) Brady is believed to be friendly with Chelsea co-owner Behdad Eghbali, who will have a big decision to make on Alonso’s future if results do not improve soon. Chelsea are languishing in eighth place after a fifth defeat in their 11 league games under Alonso, who was hyped as the stabilising force the club needed after a turbulent period. Alonso has been hampered by the absence of injured Brazilian striker Joao Pedro in recent weeks, and once again Chelsea struggled without their attacking talisman. Making his full debut in Alonso’s latest bid to find a stand-in for Pedro, Emmanuel Emegha fired Chelsea ahead in the 25th minute. Yet within three minutes they gifted an equaliser to Noah Okafor, who punished static defending to lash home. Morgan Rogers conceded a penalty eight minutes into the second half, and Dominic Calvert-Lewin converted to put Leeds in front. Swiss striker Okafor quickly made it three in the 58th minute and Brenden Aaronson got a fourth in stoppage time to leave Chelsea in turmoil. Over a miserable five-match spell, the Blues have lost to Tottenham, Sunderland and Leeds, while also crashing out of the League Cup against Liverpool. While it is too soon to suggest Alonso is in danger of the sack, the Spaniard has endured a disappointing start to his first spell as a Premier League manager. Failing to beat struggling pair Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace in their next two games would undoubtedly turn the heat up on the former Real Madrid and Bayer Leverkusen boss.
